 Brazoria County District Court
 Cause No. 2025-CV-0001
 David May, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Oral Deposition of David May
Date:
December 27, 2025
Location:
Offices of Carter & Smith Injury Lawyers
Examining attorney:
Marilyn Fox, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defending attorney:
Carlos Fox, Carter & Smith Injury Lawyers
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record, if that's acceptable. You can refer to me as the plaintiff.
Q: We can work with that for now. Where were you on the day of the collision?
A: I was driving through an intresection in Pearland, Texas. I was making a left turn across the opposing lanes, going toward a
shopping center.
Q: Tell me what you saw before the impact.
A: I checked for oncoming traffic and saw a gap. I started to turn, and then a vehicle came through much faster than I expected. I
couldn't avoid it. It struck the front passenger side of my car.
Q: Did you have a green light?
A: I had a green arrow for the left turn, as far as I recall. I'd want to look at the signal timing to be certain, but that's my memory
of it.
Q: What happened to your body when the impact occurred?
A: My head snapped forward and then back. The seatbelt caught me, but my neck felt like it had been wrenched. I had a headache
within the hour and stiffness the next morning.
Q: When did you first seek medical care?
A: The same day, at an urgent care clinic. They took X-rays and told me I had soft tissue strain in my neck. They gave me a
prescription for muscle relaxers and told me to follow up.
Q: Have you continued treatment since then?
A: Yes. I went to physical therapy about three times a week for several weeks. I also had a few visits with my primary care
doctor, who checked my range of motion.
Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?
A: It's hard to sleep on my left side, and I can't turn my head to check blind spots without pain. I used to coach my kid's soccer
team on weekends, and I had to hand that over to my spouse for a while. Lifting groceries and carrying laundry also aggravates it.
Q: Has anything improved?
A: Some. The stiffness is better in the mornings than it was. The headacehs come less often now, but I still get them when I've
been at a desk for a long stretch.
Q: Have you had any prior neck or back complaints?
A: I had some occasional stiffness years ago after sleeping wrong, but nothing that required a doctor or time off work.
</page>
